components.gap: Durrett's Thm 4.1.17 (p. 215) asserts existence for every nice (S,S): a 1-1 map phi from S into R with phi and phi^{-1} measurable (definition p. 53), with no requirement that phi(S) be Borel; its proof uses B = phi(A) = (phi^{-1})^{-1}(A) in R, a step that needs the image to be Borel. The theorem substitutes the narrower hypothesis of a coding onto a Borel set E and says it supplies 'the source's standard Borel case', and countable-product-measures.tex (lines 173-179) equates 'nice' with that class; the source's own hypothesis, the image step in its proof, and the status of the theorem for nice spaces whose image is not Borel are not addressed on the input route.

components.gap: The densities, independence and the nonuniform conditional angle law are proved and verified. Not supplied: the source presents Ex. 4.1.8 as 'Borel's paradox' (p. 210): for a randomly chosen point on the earth it might seem at first that the longitude and the great-circle angle are both uniform; the longitude is uniform but the angle is not, and 'the paradox completely evaporates' once one sees that the angle is independent of the longitude, so the conditional law is the unconditional one, nonuniform 'since there is more land near the equator than near the North Pole'. The handbook names neither the paradox nor this framing and explanation; 'Borel's paradox' is not named for this example anywhere on the input route.

Durrett (p. 214) states that r.c.d.'s do not always exist, attributes the first example to Dieudonne (1948) with references to Doob (1953, p. 624) and Faden (1985), and explains the source of the problem: countable additivity holds only a.s. for each disjoint sequence, so exceptional sets may pile up when S has enough countable disjoint collections. The boundary says only that the existence result 'is not an assertion for every measurable outcome space'; the on-route a.e.-kernels chapter records the bare nonexistence (conditioning-independence-and-information-w02b-p15-008.tex lines 233-236) without the attribution, the references or the explanation.
